inputs.text: The “No Kings” organizers say 8 million people took part across more than 3,300 events in all 50 states, though authorities have provided no official count. That estimate isn’t a national mandate—but neither is a ballot box a reason to dismiss people exercising their right to protest. Treating mass dissent as an attempt to “undo an election” is a way to silence criticism while pretending formal institutions alone guarantee justice. The organizers say turnout exceeded October’s protests by about one million people and 600 events; that scale signals real concern, not a claim to speak for everyone. A healthy democracy needs lawful transitions, but it also needs room for people to challenge power and demand institutions that protect everyone.
